readings.title: This quantum battery upends the rules of charging
body: 16 hours ago Share Save Add as preferred on Google Laurie Clarke Scientists have made the world's first quantum battery prototype and, unlike conventional batteries, it charges faster the larger it gets. Could these bizarre devices one day power quantum computing – or even your phone? Everyone knows that the larger the battery, the longer it takes to charge – that's why it can take several hours to charge a laptop and typically all night to charge an electric vehicle. That's the world we're familiar with, anyway. But in the world of the very small, different rules apply. Quantum mechanics (the science of matter at atomic and subatomic scales) "sort of flips [that] on its head", says James Quach, a quantum science researcher at Csiro, Australia's national science agency. Quach is working to create a quantum battery that defies common sense by charging faster the bigger it gets. Just as some expect quantum computers to one day revolutionise computing, Quach argues that quantum batteries could be similarly disruptive. In March 2026, his team made an important breakthrough when they unveiled what they say is the world's first working quantum battery prototype. The field is still in its infancy, and quantum technology is inherently tricksy. But some scientists say these batteries could one day power quantum devices, while the strongest advocates insist they could even be used to charge everyday devices like phones.  Others, though, remain strongly sceptical about their real-world viability.  Conventional batteries rely on chemical reactions that send 10 billion billion electrons or more rushing through the device they're powering. It sounds impressive, but some now see the technology as outdated.  "Despite major technological improvements, modern batteries still rely on electrochemical processes first explored over two centuries ago," says Dario Ferraro, associate professor of physics at the University of Genova, Italy.  This has led some researchers to look towards quantum batteries – batteries that are powered by quantum effects, rather than chemical reactions. The key point is that quantum batteries are not about storing a great amount of energy, but about delivering it faster and with greater control – Dario Ferraro The world of the very small is an overwhelmingly odd one. And quantum mechanics is no stranger to mind-bending concepts, from "entangled" particles that influence each other at great distances to time that flows backwards . The research that laid the groundwork for quantum batteries was initially driven by curiosity about which laws of classical physics might be upended in the quantum world. A milestone paper in 2015 showed that quantum entanglement means quantum batteries might charge – and discharge – more efficiently  than conventional ones.  "The key point is that quantum batteries are not about storing a great amount of energy, but about delivering it faster and with greater control," says Ferraro.   Quach has tested one way of harnessing these quantum effects to power a battery. He uses an optical microcavity, an experimental set-up where two tiny mirrors are placed 100nm apart (a width about a thousand times thinner than a human hair). He fills the tiny space between the mirrors with organic dye molecules, then beams in a laser. Using this method, the light and the molecules become strongly coupled, forming hybrid light-matter states, which enhances the system's ability to absorb and store energy – an effect known as superabsorption. It's superabsorption that's responsible for the battery's most surprising property. In classical physics, molecules are little individualists – each acting on its own and absorbing energy at a rate independent of the molecules around it. But with quantum effects, they're a little more collectivist: they "act in unison and synergise", says Quach. "So that the rate at which you can absorb energy increases with the number of molecules there are." It means that the more molecules there are (i.e. the bigger the battery) the faster it charges. Quach's prototype took femtoseconds (quadrillionths of a second) to charge, and stored the energy for nanoseconds, about six orders of magnitudes longer.   This feat was first demonstrated by Quach and his team in 2022. In March 2026 , they added a new layer, managing to extract an electrical current from the prototype. At greater intensities, this current could potentially be used to charge devices.   Quach's optical microcavity method isn't the only way to make a quantum battery. Another approach, for example, uses superconductive materials – already widely used in quantum computing. One big advantage of Quach's design, though, is that it works at room temperature. Superconductive designs only work at cryogenic temperatures starting below -150C (-238F). "This is fine for quantum computers, but not so useful to power your mobile phone," says Quach.   "If the goal is proving the quantum charging advantage as real physics… the optical microcavity route is the strongest bet," says Mauro Paternostro, a quantum physicist at Queen's University Belfast. But in the long term, Paternostro believes that the superconductive design might have the edge for practical uses, because it is easier to extract energy from. "A microcavity gives you a beautiful ensemble demonstration, but poor control over getting the energy back out in a useful, directed form."   Quach's latest experiment represents a first tentative step towards a quantum battery that could one day be substituted for conventional ones. However, at present, the prototype battery can only hold a very small amount of energy – a few billion electron volts – for a matter of nanoseconds. To power conventional devices, it would need to store far more energy for far longer. Quach says he has in fact already achieved this with a new design he's built, and is now working on a paper to publish the results. It uses "a hybrid structure", he says, involving quantum components to allow super-fast charging with classical layers added in to store the energy for longer. He also plans to combine many microscopic quantum batteries together to increase their total capacity. "If we do those two things, then we're on our way to be able to power a conventional device," he says. Still, other scientists remain sceptical, given quantum effects are notoriously fragile and are easily disrupted by observation or interference. "Interactions with the environment can quickly degrade [quantum] effects, limiting both performance and scalability," says Ferraro, which could offset part of the expected benefit of quantum batteries. Addressing this is "crucial to moving quantum batteries from theory to real-world applications", he adds.  Advancements in quantum batteries – if they are ever achieved – will likely impact quantum computing first. Quantum computers promise to one day execute tasks more rapidly than the fastest supercomputers , and technologists have warned they could threaten encryption globally . Others, though, are more sceptical: a recent paper , for example, named quantum computers alongside fusion energy and brain-computer interfaces as being among the technologies perpetually described as "five years away". More like this: • How China won the world's EV battery race • The batteries powering the world's fastest racing EVs • The liquid air alternative to fossil fuels Quach, however, argues that he is likely to achieve the powering of quantum devices with quantum batteries in his lab within the next few years. If possible, this could reduce the amount of energy quantum computers consume, as well as making them faster and less error-prone, allowing them to be scaled up faster, he claims.  Quach is less certain about using them to power conventional devices. It should one day be viable, he says, noting the fact the battery is charged with a laser means it could potentially "charge electric vehicles on-the-go". This would avoid the need for drivers to stop to recharge altogether.  Ferraro, however, is sceptical that quantum batteries could ever become the norm outside of quantum applications. "In my view… quantum batteries are unlikely to replace conventional batteries in everyday applications such as mobile phones or electric vehicles," he says. "Their natural domain is the quantum scale."   The big unsolved problem right now, says Paternostro, is making use of the quantum charging advantage while also withdrawing the energy in a controlled, usable state. Whoever achieves this, he says, "will have made the real breakthrough". -- For more insights, sign up to our Tech Decoded newsletter, where Lily Jamali and Thomas Germain break down the biggest stories of the tech world, and help you live a better digital life. ##段落
16小时前 分享 保存 设为Google首选 Laurie Clarke 科学家制造出了世界上首个量子电池原型，与传统电池不同，这种电池体积越大充电越快。这些奇特的装置有朝一日能为量子计算甚至你的手机供电吗？众所周知，电池越大，充电时间越长——这就是为什么给笔记本电脑充电需要几个小时，而给电动汽车充电通常需要一整夜。这是我们熟悉的世界。但在微观世界里，适用的是不同规则。澳大利亚国家科学机构CSIRO的量子科学研究员James Quach表示，量子力学（原子和亚原子尺度上的物质科学）“某种程度上颠覆了这一点”。Quach正致力于制造一种反常识的量子电池，其体积越大充电越快。正如一些人期望量子计算机有朝一日彻底改变计算领域一样，Quach认为量子电池同样可能带来颠覆性变革。2026年3月，他的团队取得了重大突破，公布了他们声称的世界首个可工作的量子电池原型。该领域仍处于起步阶段，量子技术本身就极其棘手。但一些科学家表示，这些电池有朝一日能为量子设备供电，而最坚定的支持者则坚持认为它们甚至可以为手机等日常设备充电。不过，其他人对其实际可行性仍持强烈怀疑态度。

##段落
传统电池依赖化学反应，将100亿亿个或更多电子送入所供电的设备。这听起来令人印象深刻，但现在一些人认为这项技术已经过时。意大利热那亚大学物理学副教授Dario Ferraro表示：“尽管技术取得了重大进步，但现代电池仍依赖于两个多世纪前首次探索的电化学过程。”这促使一些研究者将目光投向量子电池——一种由量子效应而非化学反应驱动的电池。关键在于，量子电池不是关于储存大量能量，而是关于更快、更可控地释放能量——Dario Ferraro。微观世界是一个极其奇异的世界。量子力学对令人费解的概念并不陌生，从在远距离上相互影响的“纠缠”粒子到时间倒流。为量子电池奠定基础的研究最初源于好奇心：经典物理学的哪些定律可能在量子世界中被颠覆。2015年一篇里程碑式的论文表明，量子纠缠意味着量子电池可能比传统电池更高效地充电和放电。

关键点在于，量子电池并非旨在储存大量能量，而是以更快速度和更强控制力释放能量，费拉罗如是说。夸赫已测试了一种利用这些量子效应为电池供能的方法。他采用光学微腔实验装置，其中两面微型镜子相隔100纳米（宽度约为人发千分之一）。他在镜间微小空间填充有机染料分子，随后用激光照射。通过此法，光与分子强烈耦合，形成光-物质混合态，增强系统吸收和储存能量的能力——此效应称为超吸收。正是超吸收赋予电池最惊人的特性。在经典物理中，分子如同个体主义者，各自独立运作，以与周围分子无关的速率吸收能量。但在量子效应下，它们变得更加集体主义：分子“协同行动并产生协同效应”，夸赫说，“因此能量吸收速率随分子数量增加而提升。”这意味着分子越多（即电池越大），充电越快。夸赫的原型在飞秒（千万亿分之一秒）内完成充电，能量储存持续纳秒，约长六个数量级。

这一成就最初由夸赫及其团队于2022年展示。2026年3月，他们新增一层，成功从原型中提取电流。在更高强度下，此电流有望用于为设备充电。夸赫的光学微腔方法并非制造量子电池的唯一途径。例如，另一种方法使用超导材料——这类材料已广泛应用于量子计算。然而，夸赫设计的一大优势是可在室温下运行。超导设计仅能在低于-150摄氏度（-238华氏度）的低温环境下工作。“这对量子计算机没问题，但对给手机供电不太实用，”夸赫说。

“若目标是证明量子充电优势是真实物理现象……光学微腔路线是最强选择，”贝尔法斯特女王大学量子物理学家毛罗·帕特诺斯特罗表示。但长期来看，帕特诺斯特罗认为超导设计在实用方面可能更有优势，因其更易于提取能量。“微腔提供了优美的集合演示，但在以有用、定向形式回收能量方面控制力较弱。”夸赫的最新实验是迈向未来可能替代传统电池的量子电池的初步尝试。然而，目前该原型

这种类型的电池只能容纳极少的能量——仅有几十亿电子伏特——持续时间仅为纳秒级。要驱动常规设备，它需要储存多得多的能量并维持更长时间。夸赫表示，他实际上已经通过自己设计的一种新方案实现了这一点，目前正在撰写论文以发表这些结果。他说，该方案采用“混合结构”，包含量子组件以实现超快充电，同时加入经典层来延长能量储存时间。他还计划将许多微型量子电池组合在一起，以提升总容量。“如果我们做到这两点，就能朝着驱动常规设备的方向迈进，”他说。尽管如此，其他科学家仍持怀疑态度，因为量子效应以脆弱著称，极易因观测或干扰而受到破坏。“与环境相互作用会迅速降解[量子]效应，限制其性能和可扩展性，”费拉罗说，这可能会抵消量子电池预期收益的一部分。他补充说，解决这一问题“对于将量子电池从理论推向实际应用至关重要”。

量子电池的进展——如果真能实现的话——可能首先影响量子计算领域。量子计算机有望有朝一日比最快的超级计算机更快地执行任务，技术人员也警告称它们可能威胁全球加密技术。然而，其他人则更为怀疑：例如，最近一篇论文将量子计算机与聚变能源和脑机接口并列为那些总被描述为“还有五年就能实现”的技术。更多类似内容：• 中国如何赢得全球电动车电池竞赛 • 为全球最快电动赛车提供动力的电池 • 替代化石燃料的液态空气方案

然而，夸赫辩称，他很可能在未来几年内就在实验室中用量子电池为量子设备供电。他声称，如果可能的话，这能减少量子计算机的能耗，同时使其更快、更不易出错，从而加速其扩展进程。对于将量子电池用于常规设备，夸赫则不那么确定。他说，有朝一日这应该可行，并指出电池通过激光充电的事实意味着它可能“在行驶中为电动车充电”，从而完全避免驾驶员停车充电的需求。但费拉罗却怀疑量子电池能否在量子应用之外成为常态。“在我看来……量子电池不太可能取代日常应用中的传统电池，比如手机或电动车，”他说，“它们的天然领域是量子尺度。”帕特表示，当前一个未解决的大问题是。

nostro正在利用量子充电优势，同时以可控、可用的状态提取能量。他说，无论谁实现了这一点，“都将取得真正的突破”。——欲获取更多见解，请订阅我们的《科技解码》通讯，Lily Jamali和Thomas Germain将在其中剖析科技界重大新闻，助你过上更美好的数字生活。在此免费订阅。欲获取更多来自BBC的科学、技术、环境与健康故事，请在Facebook和Instagram上关注我们。技术 电池 物理 交通 科学 专题

readings.title: The Supreme Court just revived Trump’s attempt to sabotage the 2026 election
body: Politics The Supreme Court just revived Trump’s attempt to sabotage the 2026 election The bizarre, but temporary, new voting rights decision, explained. by Ian Millhiser Aug 24, 2026, 11:15 PM UTC Gift President Donald Trump greats Chief Justice John Roberts, and Justices Elena Kagan, Brett Kavanaugh, and Amy Coney Barrett as he arrives for the State of the Union address on February 24, 2026. Win McNamee/Getty Images Ian Millhiser is a senior correspondent at Vox, where he focuses on the Supreme Court, the Constitution, and the decline of liberal democracy in the United States. He received a JD from Duke University and is the author of two books on the Supreme Court. In March, President Donald Trump issued a blatantly illegal executive order claiming that he had the power to unilaterally rewrite US election law. The order threatens prosecutions against state officials who allow certain people to vote, and it also requires states to include several federally mandated design elements in the envelopes that they use to mail ballots to voters. On Monday, the Supreme Court’s Republican majority allowed that order to go into effect. All three of the Court’s Democrats dissented. Email (required) Sign Up By submitting your email, you agree to our Terms and Privacy Notice . This site is protected by reCAPTCHA and the Google Privacy Policy and Terms of Service apply. Yet while the Court’s new decision in Trump v. California is troubling, it’s not necessarily a sign that the justices will permit Trump’s illegal order to take full effect. The Court’s actual holding in California is that two lower federal courts moved too quickly when they blocked the executive order. But California does not opine on whether the order is actually legal. The Supreme Court’s decision reinstates Trump’s order for now, but there are several active cases challenging this order in the lower courts. So it is likely that a judge will issue a new decision blocking the executive order again very soon. Still, the Court’s decision to reinstate this order, even temporarily, is likely to confuse state election officials who are racing to prepare for an upcoming election. And the provision threatening prosecutions might deter these officials from doing their jobs until that provision is blocked by another court. The case concerns two sections of Trump’s March order , one of which threatens state election officials with prosecution if they allow the wrong people to vote, and the other which appears to be an attempt to sabotage voting by mail during the 2026 midterms. The first one of these, Section 2, itself contains two provisions, one of which orders the Department of Homeland Security to “compile and transmit to the chief election official of each State a list of individuals confirmed to be United States citizens who will be above the age of 18 at the time of an upcoming Federal election and who maintain a residence in the subject State.” This simple command to compile a list would be unproblematic, except that the second provision of Section 2 orders the attorney general to prioritize prosecutions against “State and local officials or any others involved in the administration of Federal elections who issue Federal ballots to individuals not eligible to vote in a Federal election.” Thus, when both provisions of Section 2 are read together, they threaten prosecutions against any state official who issues a ballot to a voter whose name does not appear on Trump’s list of approved voters. Such a threat is unconstitutional , as the Constitution gives states, and not the federal government, the power to decide who may vote in congressional and presidential elections. The justices, however, primarily split on whether to give Trump’s order a hyperliteral reading. In dissent, Justice Sonia Sotomayor argues the two clauses are clearly connected and she cites a previous Supreme Court decision warning that “[p]eople do not lightly disregard public officers’ thinly veiled threats to institute criminal proceedings against them if they do not come around.” But the majority ignores Section 2’s purpose, and instead notes that Trump’s executive order does not explicitly require states to use Trump’s list of approved voters. They also note that the executive order’s call for the Justice Department to prosecute state officials does not include any reference to Trump’s list. In any event, even the Republican justices do not hold that the Constitution permits Trump to create a list of approved voters and prosecute state officials who depart from that list. Instead, the Republicans hold that it is too soon to block Section 2. DHS must first compile its list of approved voters, or DOJ must actually prosecute someone, before a challenge to Trump’s new policy can proceed. The effect of the Republican justices’ decision, in other words, is to leave Trump’s threat in place, but also water it down considerably: The Court does state that Trump’s executive order does not actually require states to use Trump’s approved voter list. So that may be a sign that, if Trump actually did try to prosecute someone for allowing someone not on DHS’s list to vote, the justices would reject that prosecution — but for now, there’s little standing in the way of him doing it. The remainder of the Court’s decision deals with Section 3 of Trump’s executive order, which orders the United States Postal Service (USPS) to design an envelope which states must use when they mail ballots to voters. It also forbids USPS from delivering ballots that do not comply with this new design. The Republican justices conclude that the lower court decisions blocking Section 3 were also premature because, at the time when those courts handed down their decisions, USPS had not yet formally issued a rule that announces the new mandatory envelope design. But USPS issued that rule on Friday . So the Supreme Court’s decision was out of date days before the justices decided it, but that does nothing to change the immediate effect of the decision. Among other things, the Trump administration’s new rule requires states to mail ballots in envelopes that include several federally mandated design elements, including a mandatory logo and a unique identifier for each voter. If the new rule takes effect, USPS will refuse to deliver any ballots that do not comply with these new, Trump-approved design requirements. Democrats are significantly more likely to vote by mail than Republicans. So the Trump administration’s new rule is likely to skew the 2026 election towards his political party if it is allowed to take effect. If Section 3 is eventually allowed to take effect, that will be a catastrophe for US democracy, and may even make it impossible for many states to hold midterm elections. That’s because the states couldn’t possibly have known what specific design requirements the Trump administration would impose on them until USPS issued its rule. Many states have already purchased envelopes that do not comply with the new federal mandate. And it’s not like new envelopes can simply be printed on the fly. In some states, millions or even tens of millions of voters will vote by mail , which means that, in order to comply with the Trump administration’s new order, these states will somehow need to obtain truckloads of envelopes in time for this November’s election, comply with the considerable procedural requirements laid out in Trump’s order, and distribute these ballots to voters fast enough for them to actually return them by the deadline. Several US states, moreover, conduct their elections almost entirely by mail . While these states often set up voting centers where voters can also vote in person , these in-person voting centers are merely a backup. And these states are unlikely to have the infrastructure, voting machines, or network of election workers that are required to run an entirely in-person election if mail-in voting fails. So Trump wants to impose impossible deadlines on many states. But Monday’s decision does not actually hold that it is legal for him to do so. Indeed, the federal judge who initially blocked Trump’s executive order has already signaled that she is likely to block the USPS’s new rule. We will find out if the Supreme Court will allow Trump to sabotage voting by mail after that new decision makes its way back to the justices. Trump’s lawyers only barely make a legal argument in favor of the new rule. After the USPS issued its new rule, Trump’s Justice Department did file a supplemental brief in the Supreme Court arguing that the new rule is lawful. But that brief is only three pages long, and its legal analysis is exceedingly thin. As Indira Talwani, one of the judges who blocked Trump’s executive order, noted in her opinion, there is no federal law that explicitly “delegates authority to control mail-in voting to USPS.” So the Trump administration must rely instead on broadly worded statutes that simply state that the Postal Service may deliver mail and take related steps that are necessary to deliver the mail. One permits USPS to adopt rules “ as may be necessary in the execution of its functions .” The other permits it to “ provide for the collection, handling, transportation, delivery, forwarding, returning, and holding of mail , and for the disposition of undeliverable mail.” And, even if these vague statutes could authorize the Trump administration to impose granular restrictions on voting by mail, the fact remains that it is impossible for many states to comply with these restrictions in 2026. Some states, such as North Carolina, are supposed to start mailing ballots at the end of next week . It would be one thing if Trump tried to impose new envelope design requirements that will take effect in future elections. But there’s simply no time for states to design compliant envelopes, get those designs approved by USPS order dozens of pallets worth of these envelopes, and distribute them to voters in time for the 2026 midterm elections. So the stakes in this dispute remain quite high. Trump has literally issued an executive order that, if implemented, might prevent many states from holding the midterm elections in the first place. But it is still unclear if this Supreme Court will allow that to happen. ##段落
政治 最高法院刚刚恢复了特朗普破坏2026年选举的企图 这项奇异但暂时的投票权新裁决，解析。作者：伊恩·米尔希瑟，2026年8月24日，晚上11:15 UTC 赠阅 2026年2月24日，总统唐纳德·特朗普在抵达国情咨文演讲现场时向首席大法官约翰·罗伯茨以及大法官埃琳娜·卡根、布雷特·卡瓦诺和艾米·科尼·巴雷特致意。Win McNamee/Getty Images 伊恩·米尔希瑟是Vox的高级记者，专注于最高法院、宪法以及美国自由民主的衰退。他拥有杜克大学的法学博士学位，并撰写了两本关于最高法院的书籍。

##段落
今年3月，总统唐纳德·特朗普发布了一项公然非法的行政命令，声称他有权单方面改写美国选举法。该命令威胁要对允许某些人投票的州官员提起公诉，还要求各州在邮寄选票给选民的信封上加入几项联邦强制指定的设计元素。周一，最高法院的共和党多数派允许该命令生效。法院的三位民主党大法官均表示反对。

##段落
电子邮件（必填） 注册 提交您的电子邮件即表示您同意我们的条款和隐私声明。本网站受reCAPTCHA保护，并适用Google隐私政策和服务条款。

##段落
然而，尽管法院在“特朗普诉加利福尼亚州”案中的新裁决令人不安，但这并不一定意味着大法官们会允许特朗普的非法命令全面生效。法院在加利福尼亚案中的实际裁决是，两个下级联邦法院在阻止该行政命令时行动过快。但该裁决并未对命令本身是否合法发表意见。最高法院的决定暂时恢复了特朗普的命令，但下级法院中仍有几起活跃案件挑战该命令。因此，很可能很快会有法官发布新裁决再次阻止该行政命令。

##段落
尽管如此，法院决定恢复该命令——即使是暂时性的——也可能让正忙于筹备即将到来的选举的州选举官员感到困惑。而威胁提起公诉的条款可能会阻止这些官员履行职责，直到该条款被另一家法院阻止为止。

##段落
该案件涉及特朗普3月命令中的两个部分，其中一部分威胁州选举官员，如果他们允许错误的人投票就提起公诉，另一部分则看似试图在2026年中期选举中破坏邮寄投票。第一部分，即第2节，本身包含两项条款，其中一项命令国土安全部“汇编并传送给每个州的最高选举官员一份经确认的非美国公民名单”。

##段落
在美国即将举行的联邦选举时年满18岁且在该州保持住所的美国公民。”这一简单的编制名单指令本无问题，但第2条第二款规定司法部长优先起诉“参与联邦选举管理的州和地方官员或任何其他向无资格在联邦选举中投票的个人发放联邦选票者”。因此，当第2条的两项规定合并解读时，它们威胁起诉任何向未出现在特朗普批准选民名单上的选民发放选票的州官员。这种威胁违宪，因为宪法赋予各州而非联邦政府决定谁可在国会和总统选举中投票的权力。然而，法官们主要分歧在于是否对特朗普的命令进行超字面解读。持异议的索尼娅·索托马约尔大法官认为这两项条款明显关联，并引用了先前最高法院的一项裁决，警告“[人们]不会轻视公职人员隐晦威胁——若不顺从便对其提起刑事诉讼”。但多数意见忽略了第2条的意图，反而指出特朗普的行政命令并未明确要求各州使用特朗普的批准选民名单。他们还指出，行政命令要求司法部起诉州官员的部分未提及特朗普的名单。无论如何，即使共和党法官也未认定宪法允许特朗普创建批准选民名单并起诉偏离该名单的州官员。相反，共和党人认为现在阻止第2条为时过早。国土安全部必须首先编制其批准选民名单，或司法部必须实际起诉某人，之后才能对特朗普新政策提出挑战。换言之，共和党法官裁决的效果是保留特朗普的威胁，但同时也大幅削弱了它：法院确实声明特朗普的行政命令并未实际要求各州使用特朗普的批准选民名单。因此，这可能是一个迹象——如果特朗普确实试图起诉允许未列入国土安全部名单者投票的人，法官们将驳回该起诉——但就目前而言，几乎没有障碍阻止他这样做。法院裁决的其余部分涉及特朗普行政命令的第3条，该命令指示美国邮政服务（USPS）设计一种各州向选民邮寄选票时必须使用的信封，并禁止USPS投递不符合新设计的选票。共和党

法官们认为，下级法院阻止第3条生效的裁决也为时过早，因为在这些法院作出裁决时，美国邮政局尚未正式发布宣布新强制性信封设计的规则。但美国邮政局上周五发布了该规则。因此，最高法院的裁决在法官们作出决定前几天就已过时，但这并不改变该裁决的即时效力。此外，特朗普政府的新规则要求各州在邮寄选票时使用包含多项联邦强制设计元素的信封，包括强制性标志和每位选民的唯一标识符。如果新规则生效，美国邮政局将拒绝投递任何不符合这些新批准的、经特朗普认可的设计要求的选票。民主党人比共和党人更可能通过邮寄方式投票。因此，如果允许特朗普政府的新规则生效，很可能会使2026年选举向有利于其政党的方向倾斜。如果第3条最终被允许生效，那将是美国民主的灾难，甚至可能使许多州无法举行中期选举。这是因为各州在美国邮政局发布规则之前，不可能知道特朗普政府会施加哪些具体设计要求。许多州已经购买了不符合新联邦规定的信封。而且新信封并非可以随意临时印制。在一些州，数百万甚至数千万选民将通过邮寄投票，这意味着，为了遵守特朗普政府的新命令，这些州需要设法及时获得成卡车的信封以应对今年11月的选举，遵守特朗普命令中规定的相当多的程序要求，并足够快地将这些选票分发给选民，以便他们能在截止日期前实际寄回。此外，美国有几个州几乎完全通过邮寄方式进行选举。虽然这些州通常设立投票中心，选民也可以亲自投票，但这些亲自投票中心只是备用方案。如果邮寄投票失败，这些州不太可能拥有运行完全亲自选举所需的基础设施、投票机或选举工作人员网络。因此，特朗普想要给许多州强加不可能完成的截止日期。但周一的裁决实际上并未认定他这样做是合法的。事实上，最初阻止特朗普行政命令的联邦法官已经表示，她可能会阻止美国邮政局的新规则。我们将看到，在这项新裁决重新提交给法官们后，最高法院是否会允许特朗普破坏邮寄投票。特朗普的律师

它几乎无法为新规提供有力的法律依据。在美国邮政总局发布新规后，特朗普的司法部确实向最高法院提交了一份补充意见书，主张该新规合法。但这份意见书仅有三页，其法律分析极其单薄。正如阻止特朗普行政令的法官之一英迪拉·塔尔瓦尼在意见中指出的，没有任何联邦法律明确“将控制邮寄投票的权力授予美国邮政总局”。因此，特朗普政府只能依赖措辞宽泛的法规，这些法规仅简单规定邮政总局可以投递邮件并采取投递所需的必要相关步骤。其中一项允许邮政总局采纳“执行其职能所必需的规则”，另一项允许其“规定邮件的收集、处理、运输、投递、转发、退回和保管，以及无法投递邮件的处置”。而且，即使这些模糊的法规能授权特朗普政府对邮寄投票施加细致限制，事实仍然是许多州在2026年不可能遵守这些限制。一些州，如北卡罗来纳州，原定于下周底开始寄送选票。如果特朗普试图施加未来选举生效的新信封设计要求，那另当别论。但各州根本没有时间设计合规信封、让这些设计获得邮政总局批准、订购大量此类信封的托盘，并及时在2026年中期选举前分发给选民。因此，这场争议的风险仍然相当高。特朗普确实发布了一项行政令，如果实施，可能首先阻止许多州举行中期选举。但尚不清楚最高法院是否允许这种情况发生。了解更多：唐纳德·特朗普 2026年中期选举 政治 最高法院 特朗普政府 投票权 用最新的Vox填字游戏让大脑休息一下 杰森·阿尔迪的悲剧 播客 无笼鸡蛋对气候更糟。这有关系吗？一个非常愤怒的加拿大的视角 想对富人征税？从死人开始。 电子邮件（必填） 订阅 提交您的电子邮件即表示您同意我们的条款和隐私声明。本网站受reCAPTCHA保护，并适用谷歌隐私政策和服务条款。 广告客户内容 来自 这是原生广告的标题

readings.title: There’s a know-it-all at every job — here’s how to deal
body: There’s a know-it-all at every job — here’s how to deal

Lucia dreaded interacting with her colleague Ray. Meetings that were scheduled for an hour would last two; once Ray started talking, he wouldn’t stop. “There’s no doubt he was a smart man,” Lucia says, “but he did little more than talk about everything he knew. He delegated almost all of his work to others.”

Most of us have dealt with a Ray, the know-it-all who is convinced they’re the smartest person in the room, hogs airtime in meetings  and has no qualms about interrupting others. They gleefully inform you of what’s right, even if they’re clearly wrong , lacking information or fail to understand the nuances of a situation.
Here are some of the signs of the know-it-all:
• Monopolizes conversations, refusing to be interrupted and talking over others
• Does not listen to or heed criticism or feedback
• Explains things that others already understand
• Rarely asks questions or displays curiosity
• Steals or doesn’t share credit for group successes

One reason know-it-alls exist in so many workplaces is that many organizations reward people who act as if they have all the answers. Do employees who state their ideas with conviction tend to get more support for those ideas at your job? If people appear uncertain, are they considered weak? In many cultures, decision-making is a competitive sport, rather than a collaborative effort, so acting like you know everything is a shrewd survival technique.
So how can you make your interactions with your know-it-all coworker not just less annoying but less damaging?
First, answer these four questions before taking action.
Question 1: Are they trying to prove something?

There’s a good chance your colleague’s egotism is compensating for some deficiency or fear. Considering their underlying insecurities may give you some clues about how to deal with them. For example, some know-it-alls might be constantly talking about what they accomplished in their last role as a way to demonstrate their value. If you understand that, you might make a point of validating the contributions they’re already making, freeing them from the need to tout their past achievements.
Question 2: Is their confidence warranted?

Your know-it-all colleague might have good reason to be confident in their assertions or claims, even if their demeanor leaves something to be desired. Could it be that their delivery is abrasive, but their underlying points have merit?
Question 3: Is bias playing a role in how I’m perceiving them?

We all hold biases about who is cut out to hold positions of power. And when someone doesn’t fit our preconceptions of leadership, we tend to question whether their confidence is justified. For example, research has shown that women of color have to prove their expertise over and over. Is the person you’re labeling as a know-it-all from an underestimated group? Do they belong to a culture or demographic that you have unconscious but negative biases about?
Question 4: Is their confidence pushing your buttons?

I admit that the stronger someone feels about something, the more I feel resistant to their argument, especially if their view threatens my values in some way. Ask yourself whether your reaction to your colleague has more to do with you than it does with them. Is it possible that you feel insecure when you compare your accomplishments to theirs? Or maybe you wish that you were as confident or sure minded as they are? Is their behavior causing real issues for you or the team? Or is it just annoying? Distinguish between statements or actions that are irritating and behavior that is preventing you from getting your work done.

After you can get a sense of where they’re coming from — and what role your preferences and biases may be playing in your attitude towards them — change your working relationship by trying one of these tactics.
Tactic 1: Appreciate what they have to offer

You may need to dig deep to find it, but there is probably some genuine knowledge or capability behind the know-it-all’s overconfidence. Sure, they may exaggerate their skills and successes but find the kernel of truth. And if the ultimate goal of their pretentiousness is approval or acceptance, your empathy and appreciation may help them let up on the “Look-how-much-I-know!” routine.

Most know-it-alls have an annoying habit of constantly interrupting people. One way to deal with it is to preemptively request that people refrain from interjecting. Before you start talking, explain how much time (roughly) you’re going to need and say something like, “Please hold any comments or questions until I’m done.” If you’re not making a formal presentation but are just having a discussion where some back-and-forth is expected, you might say instead, “Interruptions break my concentration, so I’d appreciate it if you’d let me finish my thoughts before jumping in.”
Tactic 3: When interruptions do occur, tactfully address them

If your efforts to preempt interruptions fail, address them directly. But don’t just raise your voice. That sets up a power struggle and your colleague is likely to talk louder in an attempt to drown you out. Instead, confidently say, “I’m going to finish my point, and then I’d love to hear what you have to say.”

If you don’t feel comfortable speaking up, enlist allies. It’s often easier for someone else to confront rudeness, saying something like, “I’d love to hear what Keith was saying before we move on,” or “I don’t think Madison was finished with her point.” If the know-it-all interrupts multiple people on your team, you could agree to speak up for each other when it happens.
One norm that I’ve been using when I’m teaching a workshop or giving a talk to a group where people will be interacting with one another (especially on Zoom) is to “take space, make space.”

The idea is that if you tend to be someone who stays quiet in meetings, you should challenge yourself to voice your opinions. If you’re someone who is prone to holding the floor, try to step back and make room for others to contribute. I’ve found that sharing this idea at the beginning results in a more equitably distributed meeting. This could be one of several norms you and your team agree on. Having established guidelines will discourage interruptions and make it safe for everyone to speak up.

Another irritating habit of the know-it-all is to proclaim: “Our customers expect us to deliver new features every six months.” “Sales are dropping because we aren’t quick enough to respond to complaints.” “In a year, no one will even be talking about this election.” If you’re sitting there wondering how they know that, it’s OK to ask for sources or data that back up their declarations.

每个工作场所都有一个“万事通”——教你如何应对
2023年5月30日
/
艾米·加洛
Facebook
X
LinkedIn
Reddit
WhatsApp
文辉·郑
露西亚害怕与同事雷打交道。原定一小时的会议会拖到两小时；一旦雷开始讲话，他就停不下来。“毫无疑问他是个聪明人，”露西亚说，“但他除了谈论自己所知的一切之外，几乎什么也不做。他把几乎所有工作都委派给了别人。”
我们大多数人都遇到过像雷这样的人——那种自以为是房间里最聪明的人、在会议中霸占发言时间、并且毫无顾忌地打断别人的“万事通”。他们会兴高采烈地告诉你什么是对的，即使他们明显错了、缺乏信息或未能理解情况的细微之处。
以下是“万事通”的一些典型特征：
• 垄断对话，拒绝被打断，并压过他人发言
• 不倾听或不理会批评或反馈
• 以居高临下的语气说话
• 解释别人已经理解的事情
• 很少提问或表现出好奇心
• 窃取或不分享团队成功的功劳
“万事通”在如此多的工作场所中存在，一个原因是许多组织会奖励那些表现得好像拥有一切答案的人。在你的工作中，那些坚定表达自己观点的员工是否更容易获得支持？如果人们显得不确定，他们是否被视为软弱？在许多文化中，决策是一项竞争性运动，而非协作努力，因此表现得像你什么都知道是一种精明的生存技巧。
那么，你如何让你与“万事通”同事的互动不仅不那么烦人，而且不那么有害呢？
首先，在采取行动之前，回答这四个问题。
问题1：他们是否在试图证明什么？
你的同事的自负很可能是在弥补某种缺陷或恐惧。考虑他们潜在的不安全感可能会给你一些应对他们的线索。例如，有些“万事通”可能不断谈论他们在上一份工作中取得的成就，以此展示自己的价值。如果你理解了这一点，你可能会特意肯定他们当前所做的贡献，从而让他们不必再炫耀过去的成就。
问题2：他们的自信是否有道理？
你的“万事通”同事可能对他们的断言或主张有充分的信心，即使他们的态度有所欠缺。有没有可能他们的表达方式令人不快，但他们的核心观点却有价值？
问题3：偏见是否影响了我对他们的看法？
我们所有人对谁适合担任权力职位都持有偏见。当某人不符合我们关于领导者的先入之见时，

##段落
当我们面对这类人时，往往会质疑他们的自信是否合理。例如，研究表明有色人种女性必须反复证明自己的专业能力。你贴上“万事通”标签的那个人，是否来自被低估的群体？他们是否属于你潜意识里存在负面偏见的文化或人群？

##段落
问题四：他们的自信是否触动了你的敏感神经？
我承认，一个人对某件事越坚定，我就越抵触他们的论点，尤其是当他们的观点在某种程度上威胁到我的价值观时。问问自己，你对同事的反应是否更多关乎你自己，而非他们。是不是你在拿自己的成就与他们比较时感到不安？或者你希望自己也像他们一样自信或笃定？他们的行为是否真的给你或团队带来了实际问题？还是仅仅让你感到烦恼？要区分那些令人恼火的言论或行为，与那些阻碍你完成工作的行为。

##段落
当你能够理解他们的出发点——以及你自己的偏好和偏见在对待他们的态度中扮演了什么角色——就可以尝试以下策略来改变你们的工作关系。

##段落
策略一：欣赏他们所能提供的价值
你可能需要深入挖掘才能找到，但在“万事通”的过度自信背后，很可能存在一些真正的知识或能力。当然，他们可能夸大了自己的技能和成就，但请找到其中真实的核心。如果他们装腔作势的最终目的是获得认可或接纳，那么你的同理心和欣赏也许能帮助他们放下“看我多懂！”的那套做派。

##段落
策略二：防止被打断
大多数“万事通”都有一个恼人的习惯——不断打断别人。处理方式之一是先发制人，请求大家不要插话。在开始发言前，说明你大概需要多少时间，并说类似“请在我讲完之前先不要评论或提问”的话。如果你不是在做正式演示，而只是一场需要来回交流的讨论，你也可以改为说：“打断会让我分心，所以如果你能让我把想法说完再插话，我会很感激。”

##段落
策略三：当打断确实发生时，机智地应对
如果你预防打断的努力失败了，就要直接处理。但不要只是提高音量，那会引发权力争夺，而你的同事很可能会说得更大声来试图盖过你。相反，自信地说：“我会先把我的观点说完，然后我很乐意听听你的想法。”

##段落
如果你觉得当面说出来不舒服，可以寻求盟友的帮助。通常由别人出面应对粗鲁行为会更容易，比如说——

## 段落

比如可以说：“我很想听听基思在我们继续之前说了什么”，或者“我觉得麦迪逊的观点还没说完”。如果那个“万事通”多次打断你团队里其他人的发言，你们可以商量好，在这种情况下互相帮忙出声。

## 段落

策略四：设定规则

在我主持研讨会或给需要互动的人群（尤其是在Zoom上）做演讲时，我一直使用的一个规则是“占位，也让位”。

这个理念是：如果你倾向于在会议中保持沉默，就应该挑战自己，主动表达观点。如果你容易霸占发言权，就试着退一步，给别人留出贡献的空间。我发现，在开场时分享这个理念，能让会议的发言机会分配更公平。这可以是你和团队共同商定的几条规则之一。有了明确的指南，就能减少打断行为，让每个人都能安全地畅所欲言。

## 段落

策略五：要求提供事实和数据

“万事通”的另一个恼人习惯是断言：“我们的客户期望我们每六个月推出新功能。”“销量下降是因为我们对投诉的响应不够快。”“一年之内，没人会再谈论这次选举了。”如果你坐在那里纳闷他们怎么知道这些的，完全可以要求他们提供支持这些说法的来源或数据。

这样做时要有礼貌，不要对抗。你可以这样说：“我不确定我们基于的假设和事实是否一致。在继续之前，让我们退一步，先看看数据。”

即使你那位专横的同事最初几次对这些质询反应不佳，他们也可能逐渐习惯你要求证据的做法，并在脱口而出未经证实的言论前三思。而且，要求他们解释自己是如何知道的，可能有助于他们认识到自己知识的局限，并促使他们未来多些谦逊。

## 段落

当你与“万事通”开会时，要手握确凿的事实出席。你越准备好捍卫自己的观点、反驳他们任何误导性的陈述，效果就越好。你也在强化一种重要性：基于事实的讨论优于虚张声势。

## 段落

策略六：示范谦逊与开放心态

许多爱炫耀的人之所以如此行事，是因为这过去对他们有效，或者因为他们或明或暗地接受到一种信息：展现自信正是你的团队、组织或他们所属文化所期望的。你可以通过展现谦逊和开放心态来提供一种不同的榜样。试着说“我不知道”或“我现在没有那个信息；我回头再告诉你”。

如果“万事通”看到你表达不确定性并不会带来什么后果，他们或许也会开始质疑自己是否真的需要时刻显得全知全能。

他们可能也愿意这样做。你甚至可以通过鼓励每个人在开会前就想要提出的解决方案或想法深思熟虑其利弊，来促使他们更加谦逊。或者，你可以提出这样的问题：
• 还有哪些其他观点？
• 如果我们尝试从另一个角度看这个问题，我们会怎么想？
• 这种方法有哪些好处和风险？

由于一些“万事通”寻求认可，简单地肯定他们的想法就能防止他们哗众取宠。在分享你的观点或提出疑问之前，感谢他们分享想法，或强调你欣赏他们观点的几点。例如，你可以说：“这个观点很有用。我同意你所说的第一部分，对第二部分我有略微不同的看法。让我们详细讨论一下。”

与“万事通”共事，轻则令人恼火，重则影响职业生涯。但你无需坐视不理或默默忍受。你可以采取措施来遏制同事的夸夸其谈，或至少减轻其对你和他人的影响。

dialogs.title: At the check-in counter
dialogs.goal: 练习护照/行李/座位相关表达，从容应对值机

lines.en: Good morning. May I see your passport and booking reference, please?
lines.zh: 早上好，请出示您的护照和预订编号。

lines.en: Sure, here you are. I'd like a window seat if possible.
lines.zh: 好的，给您。如果可以的话我想要靠窗的座位。

lines.en: I can arrange that. Are you checking in any bags today?
lines.zh: 可以安排。您今天有要托运的行李吗？

lines.en: Just one suitcase. Does it meet the weight limit?
lines.zh: 就一个行李箱。它超重了吗？

lines.en: It's within the limit. Your boarding pass is ready — gate 22, boarding at 10:40.
lines.zh: 在限额内。您的登机牌好了——22 号登机口，10:40 登机。

lines.en: Great. Could you also confirm that my carry-on bag fits the cabin size requirements?
lines.zh: 太好了。您能再确认一下我的随身行李符合客舱尺寸要求吗？

lines.en: Let me check the dimensions. Yes, it fits within our standard allowance. You're all set for the cabin.
lines.zh: 让我看一下尺寸。是的，符合我们的标准限额。您的客舱行李没问题。

lines.en: Perfect. By the way, is there any chance I could get an aisle seat instead? I just realized I may need to stretch my legs.
lines.zh: 太好了。顺便问一下，我能改成过道座位吗？我刚意识到可能需要伸伸腿。

lines.en: Certainly. Let me update that for you — I've moved you to 21C, an aisle seat. No problem at all.
lines.zh: 当然可以。我来为您更新——已为您调到21C，过道座位。完全没问题。

lines.en: Thank you so much. One last thing — what time should I be at the gate?
lines.zh: 非常感谢。最后问一下，我应该在什么时间到登机口？

lines.en: Please be at the gate at least 30 minutes before boarding. Enjoy your flight, and have a wonderful trip!
lines.zh: 请在登机前至少30分钟到达登机口。祝您飞行愉快，旅途顺利！

dialogs.title: Small talk at a conference
dialogs.goal: 用自然的破冰句开启商务对话，并过渡到合作话题

lines.en: Hi, I don't think we've met. I'm Echo, from the consumer insights team.
lines.zh: 你好，我们好像还没见过。我是 Echo，来自消费者洞察团队。

lines.en: Nice to meet you. I work on product strategy. What brings you to this session?
lines.zh: 很高兴认识你。我做产品策略。你为什么来听这场？

lines.en: I'm exploring how AI is changing our research methods. Have you seen anything useful today?
lines.zh: 我在研究 AI 如何改变我们的研究方法。你今天有看到什么有用的吗？

lines.en: Actually, yes — a talk on real-time consumer signals. We should compare notes sometime.
lines.zh: 其实有——一个关于实时消费者信号的演讲。我们应该找个时间交流一下。

lines.en: I'd love that. Let's grab coffee after the keynote.
lines.zh: 太好了。主题演讲后我们喝杯咖啡吧。

lines.en: Sounds good. By the way, how does your team currently handle qualitative data?
lines.zh: 听起来不错。顺便问一下，你们团队目前是怎么处理定性数据的？

lines.en: We still rely heavily on manual coding, which is time-consuming. That's why I'm keen on AI-driven tools.
lines.zh: 我们还是主要靠人工编码，很耗时。所以我对 AI 驱动的工具很感兴趣。

lines.en: Interesting. We've been piloting a sentiment analysis model that might complement your workflow.
lines.zh: 有意思。我们一直在试点一个情绪分析模型，可能和你们的工作流互补。

lines.en: That sounds promising. Could you share a bit more about how it handles multilingual data?
lines.zh: 听起来很有前景。你能多分享一下它如何处理多语言数据吗？

lines.en: Sure — it's trained on several major languages, but accuracy varies. Maybe we can set up a quick demo next week.
lines.zh: 当然——它在几种主要语言上训练过，但准确率有差异。也许我们下周可以安排一个快速演示。

lines.en: Perfect. I'll bring our research lead along. Let's exchange contacts and follow up by email.
lines.zh: 完美。我会带上我们的研究负责人。我们交换一下联系方式，然后邮件跟进吧。

dialogs.title: Checking into a hotel
dialogs.goal: 掌握入住登记、特殊需求与Wi-Fi等常用句

lines.en: Good evening. Do you have a reservation under the name Lee?
lines.zh: 晚上好。请问有预订在 Lee 名下吗？

lines.en: Yes, for two nights. Is breakfast included?
lines.zh: 有的，住两晚。含早餐吗？

lines.en: It is — served from 7 to 10. Could I have a room on a higher floor, away from the elevator?
lines.zh: 含的——7 点到 10 点供应。可以安排高一点、远离电梯的房间吗？

lines.en: Certainly. Here's your key card, and the Wi-Fi password is on this slip.
lines.zh: 当然可以。这是您的房卡，Wi-Fi 密码在这张纸上。

lines.en: Thank you. Could you also confirm the checkout time for me?
lines.zh: 谢谢。另外能帮我确认一下退房时间吗？

lines.en: Checkout is at noon, but we offer a late checkout until 2 PM for an additional fee.
lines.zh: 退房时间是中午12点，不过我们可以提供延迟至下午2点的退房服务，需额外收费。

lines.en: That's good to know. I might take advantage of that. Is there a gym or pool on site?
lines.zh: 这信息很有用，我可能会用到。酒店内有健身房或游泳池吗？

lines.en: Yes, both are on the second floor, open from 6 AM to 10 PM. Towels are provided at the front desk.
lines.zh: 有的，两者都在二楼，开放时间为早上6点到晚上10点。毛巾可在前台领取。

lines.en: Perfect. One more thing — could you arrange a wake-up call at 7:30 tomorrow morning?
lines.zh: 太好了。还有一件事——能帮我安排明早7:30的叫醒服务吗？

lines.en: Of course. I've noted that for room 1208. Is there anything else you need?
lines.zh: 当然可以。我已为您记录在1208房间。还有其他需要吗？

lines.en: No, that's all for now. Thanks for your help.
lines.zh: 暂时没有了，谢谢你的帮助。

dialogs.title: Ordering with dietary needs
dialogs.goal: 清晰表达过敏/忌口，避免误会

lines.en: Welcome! Have you decided what you'd like to order?
lines.zh: 欢迎！您决定好点什么了吗？

lines.en: Not yet. I'm allergic to peanuts — could you tell me which dishes are safe?
lines.zh: 还没。我对花生过敏——能告诉我哪些菜是安全的吗？

lines.en: Of course. The grilled fish and the vegetable soup are both nut-free. I'll note the allergy for the kitchen.
lines.zh: 当然。烤鱼和蔬菜汤都不含坚果。我会在厨房单上标注过敏。

lines.en: Perfect, thank you. Could I also get that without spicy sauce?
lines.zh: 太好了，谢谢。那份可以不放辣酱吗？

lines.en: Absolutely. I'll make sure the chef prepares it with a mild seasoning instead. Would you like any appetizer to start?
lines.zh: 完全可以。我会确保厨师改用清淡调味。需要先来点开胃菜吗？

lines.en: Yes, the spring rolls look good — but are they fried in peanut oil?
lines.zh: 好的，春卷看起来不错——但那是用花生油炸的吗？

lines.en: Good question. We use canola oil for frying, so they're safe. However, the dipping sauce contains sesame paste — would you like it on the side?
lines.zh: 问得好。我们用菜籽油炸，所以是安全的。不过蘸酱含芝麻酱——需要单独放旁边吗？

lines.en: That would be great. Please keep the sauce separate, and I'll decide whether to use it.
lines.zh: 那太好了。请把酱单独放，我自己决定要不要用。

lines.en: Understood. I'll also check with the kitchen on the dessert options — the mango pudding is peanut-free, but the chocolate cake may contain traces.
lines.zh: 明白了。我还会和厨房确认甜点选项——芒果布丁不含花生，但巧克力蛋糕可能含微量。

lines.en: Thanks for being so thorough. I'll go with the mango pudding then.
lines.zh: 谢谢你这么仔细。那我就选芒果布丁吧。

lines.en: Great choice. I'll place your order now and confirm everything with the chef. Your safety is our priority.
lines.zh: 好选择。我现在下单并和厨师确认所有细节。您的安全是我们的首要任务。

dialogs.title: Talking about AI at work
dialogs.goal: 用职场商务英语表达对 AI 的看法与担忧

lines.en: Have you tried the new AI assistant? It's been a game-changer for my drafts.
lines.zh: 你试过新的 AI 助手了吗？它彻底改变了我写草稿的方式。

lines.en: I have, but I'm cautious. I double-check everything it produces.
lines.zh: 试过，但我比较谨慎。它生成的东西我都会复核。

lines.en: Fair enough. I see it as a starting point, not the final answer.
lines.zh: 有道理。我把它当作起点，而不是最终答案。

lines.en: Exactly. The human touch still matters most with our clients.
lines.zh: 没错。对咱们的客户来说，人情味依然最重要。

lines.en: That said, I've noticed it saves me at least two hours a day on research and summarization.
lines.zh: 话虽如此，我注意到它每天至少帮我在研究和总结上省下两个小时。

lines.en: I can see that. But what about accuracy? I've caught it making subtle errors in data interpretation.
lines.zh: 这我能理解。但准确性呢？我抓到过它在数据解读上犯一些很细微的错误。

lines.en: I've seen that too. That's why I always cross-reference its output with our internal reports.
lines.zh: 我也遇到过。所以我才总是拿它生成的内容和咱们内部报告做交叉核对。

lines.en: Good practice. My concern is more about long-term dependency—are we losing our own analytical skills?
lines.zh: 好习惯。我更担心的是长期依赖——我们会不会失去自己的分析能力？

lines.en: That's a valid point. I try to use it as a tool, not a crutch. I still do the critical thinking myself.
lines.zh: 这点提得很对。我尽量把它当工具，而不是拐杖。关键思考还是我自己来。

lines.en: I think we need a team guideline on when and how to use AI, especially for client-facing documents.
lines.zh: 我觉得咱们需要一份团队指南，明确什么时候、怎么用 AI，尤其是面对客户的文档。

lines.en: Agreed. Let's bring that up in next week's meeting—maybe we can draft a policy together.
lines.zh: 同意。咱们下周会上提一下——也许可以一起起草一份规范。

dialogs.title: Briefing a Descriptive Panel
dialogs.zhTitle: 为描述性感官评价小组做导入简报
dialogs.goal: 掌握主持感官评价小组时的标准指令语言与"去引导化"表达。

lines.en: Good morning, everyone. Before we start, a quick reminder: we are not looking for whether you like the sample. We are looking for what you perceive.
lines.zh: 早上好。开始之前提醒一下：我们不是要知道你喜不喜欢这个样品，而是要知道你感知到了什么。

lines.en: So we should keep preference out of it entirely?
lines.zh: 所以我们要完全把偏好排除在外？

lines.en: Exactly. Intensity, not preference. If something is very sweet and you personally hate it, the score is still high.
lines.zh: 正是。评的是强度，不是喜好。如果某样东西很甜而你个人讨厌它，分数依然要打高。

lines.en: Understood. And the order of the samples?
lines.zh: 明白了。样品顺序呢？

lines.en: Balanced and randomised, as always. Please cleanse your palate with water and the unsalted cracker between each one, and wait ninety seconds.
lines.zh: 照例是平衡随机化的。每个样品之间请用清水和无盐饼干清口，并等待 90 秒。

lines.en: What if I pick up an attribute that is not on the ballot?
lines.zh: 如果我感知到一个评分表上没有的属性怎么办？

lines.en: Write it in the open field. Honestly, those are often the most useful lines on the whole sheet.
lines.zh: 写在开放栏里。说实话，那些往往是整张表上最有价值的内容。

lines.en: Should I try to match the vocabulary we agreed on in training?
lines.zh: 我需要尽量用我们培训时统一的词汇吗？

lines.en: Use the lexicon where it fits, but do not force it. A forced term hides more than it reveals.
lines.zh: 合适的地方就用词典里的术语，但别硬套。硬套的术语掩盖的比揭示的多。

lines.en: One last thing — no discussion during evaluation. We compare notes only in the debrief.
lines.zh: 最后一点——评价过程中不要交流。我们只在总结环节比对结果。

keys.zh: 评强度，不评偏好（感官分析第一原则）
平衡随机化（样品呈送设计）

dialogs.title: Presenting Findings the Client Did Not Want
dialogs.zhTitle: 汇报一个客户不想听到的结论
dialogs.goal: 练习在坏消息中保持专业与建设性的商务表达。

lines.en: So, bottom line — does the new formulation win?
lines.zh: 所以，直接说结论——新配方赢了吗？

lines.en: Not on the measure you asked about. But I would argue you were asking about the wrong measure.
lines.zh: 在你问的那个指标上没有。但我认为，你问的可能不是该问的那个指标。

lines.en: Go on.
lines.zh: 你说。

lines.en: Overall liking is flat — statistically indistinguishable. However, the new formulation scores significantly higher on perceived care and product quality cues.
lines.zh: 总体喜好度持平，统计上无差异。但新配方在"感知到的用心程度"和"品质线索"上显著更高。

lines.en: Does that translate into anything commercial?
lines.zh: 这能转化成商业结果吗？

lines.en: It correlates strongly with repurchase intent in this category. Liking predicts the first purchase; quality cues predict the fourth.
lines.zh: 在这个品类里，它与复购意向高度相关。喜好度预测第一次购买，品质线索预测第四次。

lines.en: That is a bolder claim than I expected from you.
lines.zh: 这比我预期的你会说的话要大胆。

lines.en: It is in the appendix with the regression. I would rather show you the uncomfortable version now than the comfortable one in six months.
lines.zh: 附录里有回归结果。我宁愿现在给你看那个不舒服的版本，也不想六个月后给你看那个舒服的版本。

lines.en: Fair. What would you do if this were your decision?
lines.zh: 有道理。如果是你来定，你会怎么做？

lines.en: Ship it, but rewrite the claim. You are selling reassurance, not novelty.
lines.zh: 上市，但改掉宣称。你卖的是安心感，不是新奇感。

dialogs.title: A Tight Connection
dialogs.goal: 掌握机场改签、行李与登机口相关的高频表达。

lines.en: Excuse me, my inbound flight was delayed and I have fifty minutes to make my connection. Will I be all right?
lines.zh: 打扰一下，我来程航班延误了，中转只剩 50 分钟。来得及吗？

lines.en: It is tight but doable. Are you checked through to your final destination?
lines.zh: 有点紧但可以。您的行李是直挂到终点的吗？

lines.en: Yes, my luggage is tagged all the way through. Do I need to clear security again?
lines.zh: 是的，行李直挂到底。我需要重新过安检吗？

lines.en: You will, at the transfer point. Follow the purple signs, and mention your connection time at the desk — they can fast-track you.
lines.zh: 需要，在中转处。跟着紫色指示牌走，在柜台说明您的中转时间，他们可以帮您走快速通道。

lines.en: That is a relief. And if I miss it, what are my options?
lines.zh: 那我就放心了。万一没赶上，我有什么选择？

lines.en: You would be rebooked on the next available flight at no charge, since the delay was ours.
lines.zh: 因为延误是我们造成的，您会被免费改签到下一个有位的航班。

lines.en: Could you note my seat preference now, just in case? Aisle, towards the front.
lines.zh: 能不能现在先记下我的座位偏好，以防万一？靠走道，靠前一点。

lines.en: Noted. Here is your boarding pass. Gate B22 — boarding closes twenty minutes before departure.
lines.zh: 记下了。这是您的登机牌。B22 登机口，起飞前 20 分钟停止登机。

lines.en: Thank you. One more thing — is there anywhere to grab a quick coffee on the way?
lines.zh: 谢谢。还有一件事——路上有地方能快速买杯咖啡吗？

lines.en: There is a kiosk right past security. Honestly, with fifty minutes, I would skip it.
lines.zh: 过了安检就有个小店。不过说实话，只有 50 分钟的话，我建议您别去了。

dialogs.title: Explaining What You Do at a Dinner Party
dialogs.zhTitle: 在饭局上解释你到底是做什么的
dialogs.goal: 练习用非专业语言介绍专业工作，这是最难也最有用的能力。

lines.en: So what do you actually do? Something with market research?
lines.zh: 你到底是做什么的？跟市场调研有关？

lines.en: Sort of. I work on how products feel — taste, texture, smell — and why people prefer one over another.
lines.zh: 算是吧。我研究产品给人的感受——味道、质地、气味——以及人们为什么更偏爱其中一个。

lines.en: Wait, that is a real job? Who pays for that?
lines.zh: 等等，这是个真实存在的职业？谁会为这个付钱？

lines.en: Anyone who makes something you put in your mouth or on your skin. If two products cost the same, the one that feels right wins.
lines.zh: 任何做入口或上脸产品的公司。两个产品价格一样，感觉对的那个就赢了。

lines.en: Give me an example.
lines.zh: 举个例子。

lines.en: Sure. Think about the sound a jar makes when you first open it. That pop is engineered, and it makes the food taste fresher.
lines.zh: 好。想想第一次拧开一个罐子时的声音。那声"啵"是设计出来的，它会让食物尝起来更新鲜。

lines.en: You are telling me I have been manipulated by a lid.
lines.zh: 你是说我一直在被一个盖子操纵。

lines.en: I would say informed by a lid. Your brain uses every clue it can get, and sound is a very cheap clue.
lines.zh: 我会说是被一个盖子"告知"了。你的大脑会用上一切能拿到的线索，而声音是最廉价的一种。

lines.en: Does knowing all this ruin it for you?
lines.zh: 知道这些会不会让你失去乐趣？

lines.en: Occasionally. But mostly it does the opposite — it turns an ordinary Tuesday breakfast into something worth paying attention to.
lines.zh: 偶尔会。但大多数时候是反过来的——它让一个普通周二的早餐变成值得留意的东西。

keys.en: the one that feels right wins

keys.zh: 被操纵 / 被告知（一组有分寸感的对比）

dialogs.title: Pushing Back on an Impossible Timeline
dialogs.zhTitle: 拒绝一个不可能的排期
dialogs.goal: 练习职场中"有边界感但不对抗"的英文表达。

lines.en: We need the consumer test results by the fifteenth. Can you make that work?
lines.zh: 我们需要在 15 号前拿到消费者测试结果。你能做到吗？

lines.en: Let me walk you through what fifteenth would require, and then you can decide.
lines.zh: 我先带你过一遍 15 号意味着什么，然后你来决定。

lines.en: Okay.
lines.zh: 好。

lines.en: Recruitment alone is eight working days for this profile. That leaves two days for fieldwork and one for analysis.
lines.zh: 光是招募��类人群就要 8 个工作日。剩下 2 天做执行，1 天做分析。

lines.en: Could we shorten recruitment?
lines.zh: 招募能压缩吗？

lines.en: We could, but then we take whoever is available, and 'whoever is available' is a real bias, not a rounding error.
lines.zh: 可以，但那样我们只能要"谁有空要谁"，而"谁有空"是一个真实的偏差，不是舍入误差。

lines.en: What would you propose?
lines.zh: 你的建议是？

lines.en: Two options. A directional read on the fifteenth with a clear health warning, or a defensible result on the twenty-second.
lines.zh: 两个选项。15 号给一个方向性判断，并附明确的局限说明；或者 22 号给一个经得起挑战的结论。

lines.en: The steering committee meets on the eighteenth.
lines.zh: 指导委员会 18 号开会。

lines.en: Then take the directional read, and let me write the caveat slide myself. If someone quotes it out of context in a board deck, we both pay for it.
lines.zh: 那就用方向性判断，但局限说明那页让我自己写。如果有人把它断章取义放进董事会材料，我们两个都要付代价。

lines.en: Deal.
lines.zh: 成交。

keys.zh: 方向性判断（非定论性结论）
不是可以忽略的小误差

dialogs.title: A Room With a Problem
dialogs.goal: 练习礼貌而坚定的投诉与协商。

lines.en: Hi, I checked in about an hour ago into 704. I am afraid the room is not going to work.
lines.zh: 你好，我大约一小时前入住 704。恐怕这个房间不太行。

lines.en: I am sorry to hear that. May I ask what the issue is?
lines.zh: 很抱歉。方便问一下是什么问题吗？

lines.en: There is a persistent smell of damp, and the air conditioning is quite loud. I have an early start tomorrow.
lines.zh: 有一股持续的潮味，空调也挺吵。我明天要早起。

lines.en: Let me see what else we have. We are fairly full tonight.
lines.zh: 我看看还有什么房。今晚我们几乎满房。

lines.en: I appreciate that. I am not asking for an upgrade — just somewhere quiet and dry.
lines.zh: 我理解。我不是要求升级——只想要一个安静干燥的房间。

lines.en: I can offer you 1102. It is a similar layout, higher floor, away from the lift shaft.
lines.zh: 我可以给您 1102。户型相近，楼层更高，远离电梯井。

lines.en: That sounds much better. Could someone help me move the bags?
lines.zh: 那好多了。能安排人帮我搬一下行李吗？

lines.en: Of course. And I will note a late checkout on your booking for the inconvenience.
lines.zh: 当然。另外我会在您的订单上备注延迟退房，作为对不便的补偿。

lines.en: That is very kind — thank you for sorting it out so quickly.
lines.zh: 太贴心了——谢谢你这么快就处理好。

lines.en: You are most welcome. I will have the bellman bring up your new key shortly.
lines.zh: 不客气。我会让行李员马上把新房卡送上去。

lines.en: Perfect. I will head up now and get settled. Thanks again for your help.
lines.zh: 太好了。我现在就上去安顿。再次感谢你的帮助。

keys.en: I am not asking for an upgrade
keys.zh: 我并不是要求升级（降低对抗感）

dialogs.title: Small Talk at a Conference Coffee Break
dialogs.zhTitle: 会议茶歇上的专业闲聊
dialogs.goal: 练习从寒暄自然过渡到有价值的专业交流。

lines.en: That last session was a bit of a sales pitch, was it not?
lines.zh: 刚那场基本就是个推销吧？

lines.en: A little. Though the bit about implicit measurement was worth staying for.
lines.zh: 有一点。不过关于内隐测量的那一段还是值得留下来听的。

lines.en: Are you on the client side or agency?
lines.zh: 你是甲方还是乙方？

lines.en: Client side — I look after sensory and consumer insights for a personal care portfolio.
lines.zh: 甲方——我负责一个个护品类组合的感官与消费者洞察。

lines.en: Then you must be dealing with the AI question constantly.
lines.zh: 那你肯定天天在面对 AI 那个问题。

lines.en: Constantly. My working position is that AI is excellent before fieldwork and dangerous after it.
lines.zh: 天天。我目前的立场是：AI 在田野之前很好用，在田野之后很危险。

lines.en: That is a neat way of putting it. Where do you draw the line exactly?
lines.zh: 这个说法很精炼。你具体在哪里划这条线？

lines.en: Anything that generates hypotheses, yes. Anything that generates respondents, no.
lines.zh: 任何用来生成假设的，可以。任何用来生成受访者的，不行。

lines.en: I might steal that for my next steering group.
lines.zh: 我下次开指导会可能要借用一下这句。

lines.en: Please do. Are you around for the afternoon panel? I would be curious what you make of it.
lines.zh: 尽管用。你下午的圆桌还在吗？我挺想听听你怎么看。

keys.en: a bit of a sales pitch
where do you draw the line

dialogs.title: Moderating a Focus Group
dialogs.zhTitle: 主持一场焦点小组访谈
dialogs.goal: 练习在焦点小组中保持中立、追问而不引导、妥善处理冷场与分歧。

lines.en: Let's start simple — when you first tasted this, what was the very first thing that came to mind?
lines.zh: 咱们从简单处开始——你第一口尝到时，最先冒出来的念头是什么？

lines.en: It felt… clean? Like, not heavy on the tongue.
lines.zh: 感觉……很干净？就是说，舌头上不厚重。

lines.en: Clean — can you stay with that word for a second? What makes it feel clean versus, say, watery?
lines.zh: “干净”——你能就这个词再多说一点吗？它和所谓“寡淡”的区别在哪？

lines.en: For me clean means no aftertaste. Watery would be thin and forgettable.
lines.zh: 对我来说干净就是没有余味。寡淡则是单薄、喝完就忘了。

lines.en: Good distinction. Anyone feel something different in the aftertaste?
lines.zh: 这个区分很好。有人对余味有不同感受吗？

lines.en: There's a slight bitterness at the end. Not bad, just… present.
lines.zh: 尾段有一点苦。不讨厌，就是……存在感。

lines.en: Noted — a late bitterness. And does that bitterness make you want to take another sip, or stop?
lines.zh: 记下了——尾段苦。这种苦是让你想再喝一口，还是想停下？

lines.en: Actually it makes me curious. I'd go again.
lines.zh: 其实它让我有点好奇。我会再喝。

lines.en: Curious is interesting. So the bitterness isn't a reject signal here?
lines.zh: “好奇”这个点有意思。所以这里的苦并不是拒绝信号？

lines.en: No, it feels intentional. Like the product knows what it's doing.
lines.zh: 不是，它感觉是刻意的。像产品心里有数。

keys.en: first thing that came to mind

dialogs.title: Ordering at a Café
dialogs.goal: 掌握点单、定制规格、堂食外带与确认等待时间的日常高频表达。

lines.en: Hi! What can I get for you?
lines.zh: 您好！要点点什么？

lines.en: Could I get a medium flat white, please? With oat milk if you have it.
lines.zh: 麻烦来一杯中杯澳白，可以的话用燕麦奶。

lines.en: Sure — oat milk, medium flat white. Anything to eat?
lines.zh: 好的——燕麦奶，中杯澳白。要配点吃的吗？

lines.en: Maybe one of those almond croissants. Is it still warm?
lines.zh: 来一个那个杏仁可颂吧。现在还是热的吗？

lines.en: Just came out of the oven. Want it heated a little more?
lines.zh: 刚出炉。要再加热一下吗？

lines.en: That'd be great, thank you. And could I get that to stay, not takeaway?
lines.zh: 那太好了，谢谢。这杯我要堂食，不要外带。

lines.en: For here. Name for the cup?
lines.zh: 堂食。杯子写什么名字？

lines.en: It's Echo. How long should I expect to wait?
lines.zh: 写 Echo。大概要等多久？

lines.en: About four minutes — I'll bring it over to your table.
lines.zh: 大概四分钟——我给你送到座位上。

lines.en: Perfect, thanks so much.
lines.zh: 太好了，非常感谢。

dialogs.title: Negotiating a Specification With a Supplier
dialogs.zhTitle: 与供应商谈一份感官规格
dialogs.goal: 练习就感官规格、批次公差与交付节奏与供应商沟通，守住品质底线。

lines.en: So you want the sweetness capped at level 3 on your scale?
lines.zh: 所以你们希望甜度上限压在你们量表的 3 级？

lines.en: Level 3, and critically — no more than a half-step variance between batches.
lines.zh: 3 级，而且关键是——批次之间波动不能超过半级。

lines.en: Half a step is tight. That means we re-calibrate the line every run.
lines.zh: 半级很紧。那意味着每批我们都要重新校准产线。

lines.en: I understand the cost. But the consumer test showed anything above 3.5 drops purchase intent.
lines.zh: 成本我理解。但消费者测试显示，超过 3.5 购买意向就掉。

lines.en: Fair. What if we hold 3.0 to 3.3 and flag anything outside?
lines.zh: 合理。那我们控制在 3.0 到 3.3，超出的做标记，行吗？

lines.en: That works, as long as the flag triggers a hold, not a shipment.
lines.zh: 可以，前提是标记触发的是“扣留”，不是“发货”。

lines.en: Agreed — out-of-band goes to quarantine, not the truck.
lines.zh: 同意——超范围的进待检区，不上车。

lines.en: And lead time? We can't promise the same volume if batches fail.
lines.zh: 那交期呢？如果批次出问题，我们给不了同样产量。

lines.en: We'll build in a 10% buffer stock. You get first refusal on it.
lines.zh: 我们会留 10% 缓冲库存。你们有优先调配权。

lines.en: Good. Let's put the tolerance in writing before pilot.
lines.zh: 好。试点前我们把公差写进合同。

dialogs.title: Getting Directions on the Street
dialogs.goal: 掌握问路、确认距离、交通方式切换与表达感谢的实用句型。

lines.en: Excuse me, is the metro station far from here?
lines.zh: 打扰一下，地铁站离这儿远吗？

lines.en: Which one? There are two within walking distance.
lines.zh: 哪个站？步行范围内有两个。

lines.en: The one near the museum — line 4, I think.
lines.zh: 博物馆旁边那个——应该是 4 号线。

lines.en: That's about a ten-minute walk, straight down this street, then left at the church.
lines.zh: 走过去大概十分钟，沿这条街一直走，到教堂左转。

lines.en: Straight, then left at the church. And is it signposted?
lines.zh: 一直走，教堂左转。那儿有路牌指示吗？

lines.en: Mostly. But the sign's small — look up, not at the shops.
lines.zh: 基本有。但牌子小——抬头看，别盯店铺。

lines.en: Got it. Could I take a bus instead, if I get lost?
lines.zh: 明白了。万一迷路，我能坐公交吗？

lines.en: Bus 11 stops right there. But walking's quicker at this hour.
lines.zh: 11 路公交就在那儿停。不过这会儿走路更快。

lines.en: Perfect, I'll walk. Thank you, you saved me.
lines.zh: 太好了，我走过去。谢谢你，帮了大忙。

lines.en: No problem — enjoy the museum.
lines.zh: 不客气——博物馆好好玩。

dialogs.title: Scheduling a Meeting by Email
dialogs.goal: 练习礼貌提议时间、协调多人日程、提前同步议程与跟进。

lines.en: Hi Mark, hoping to sync on the Q3 research plan — do you have 30 minutes next week?
lines.zh: Mark 你好，想就三季度研究计划对齐一下——下周你有 30 分钟吗？

lines.en: Wednesday looks open. Morning your time?
lines.zh: 周三好像有空。你那边上午？

lines.en: Wednesday 10am works. Should we include Lena from insights?
lines.zh: 周三上午十点可以。要把洞察部的 Lena 也拉上吗？

lines.en: Yes, she owns the consumer data. Send the invite and I'll add her.
lines.zh: 要，消费数据是她负责的。你发邀约，我来加她。

lines.en: Done. I'll share the agenda beforehand so we don't wander.
lines.zh: 发了。我会提前发议程，免得跑题。

lines.en: Please do — last time we spent 20 minutes on the wrong slide.
lines.zh: 务必——上次我们拿错幻灯片耗了 20 分钟。

lines.en: Noted. I'll keep it to three points: scope, timeline, owners.
lines.zh: 记下了。我控制三个点：范围、时间线、责任人。

lines.en: That's the Mark I like. Anything you need from me before?
lines.zh: 这才对味。会前你需要我做什么？

lines.en: Just your take on the budget ceiling. I don't want to over-promise.
lines.zh: 就你对预算上限的看法。我不想过度承诺。

lines.en: I'll send a one-liner by Tuesday. Talk Wednesday.
lines.zh: 周二前我发一句话给你。周三聊。
